thread:
anne: Brain dump from today's design touchpoint on policy engine "rate-shaping" vs "slot-based" admission. want quick sanity checks before i file an RFC.

anne: problem statement: sudden tenant bursts cause long tail latency for mixed SLO tiers. the policy engine must trade cost and latency while providing predictable isolation.

sahil: two primitives to consider: (A) slot-based admission: allocate N concurrent slots per tenant/tier (fast, simple), (B) rate-shaping token-bucket per tenant that gates request starts (smoother but global state heavier).

maria: slot model is great for short-lived workloads but brittle for downstream variability (kv-warmups). token-bucket handles bursts better but harder to debug.

kevin: hybrid idea: have short-lived slots seeded by a token-bucket reservoir. tokens replenish at tier-defined rate; acquiring a token then grabs a slot if available; if no slot, queue up to small timeout before rejecting. minimizes queue piles.

lia: runtime boundary: all admission decisions must be O(1) and offline-cacheable. router should keep local per-tenant counters and an epoched token delta from policy service. no DB calls in hot path.

anne: API proposal for policy-service (stateless): input = tenant, region, priority, request_size_estimate. output = {allow_start:bool, slot_lease_ms:optional, expected_cost_estimate}. policy publishes per-tenant quotas and replenish rates via config feed.

devops-bot: infra: rolling canary of policy-service v0.91 started in us-west-2 at 2026-03-24T09:10Z :rocket:

maria: telemetry we need: start_denied_ratio, queue_time_ms histogram, slot_steal_count, token_replenish_variance. add per-epoch snapshot to catch regressions.

sahil: fairness rule: do not let any tenant exceed burst_capacity = base_rate * burst_multiplier for more than burst_window. burst_multiplier should be function of SLA tier. also implement a slow-start after large evictions.

kevin: slow-start detail: when a tenant is evicted due to preemption, mark it in a cooldown map with linear ramp back to full bucket over cooldown_ms. prevents thrash / cache storms.

lia: question: should region affinity be expressed as hard constraint or soft bias? e.g., prefer local region slots but allow cross-region spill with penalty.

anne: we decided soft bias is safer: penalize cross-region admission by inflating token cost (e.g., cost += region_penalty_factor). simplifies capacity accounting.

maria: edge-case: multi-tenant fanout requests that spawn many downstream model calls. we should budget per-root-request by summing estimated token_count across children. add `root_trace_id` to inputs so router can account.

kevin: proto config example to put in RFC: 

```
admissions:
  tiers:
    gold:
      base_rate: 120/s
      burst_multiplier: 2.0
      cooldown_ms: 30000
    silver:
      base_rate: 40/s
      burst_multiplier: 1.5
      cooldown_ms: 45000
  global:
    slot_count_per_node: 400
    region_penalty_factor: 1.25
    max_queue_ms: 150
```

lia: ops-runbook note: if start_denied_ratio for gold > 0.5 for >5m, auto-open runbook. include quick rollback: revert weight epoch and revert policy-service to last-good.

anne: explainability: policy-service should emit a compact trace per denied start showing contributing factors: tokens_left, slot_free, recent_evictions, region_penalty, epoch_version. TTL 5m, accessible via Console.

sahil: simulation plan: replay 7 days of production ingress, synthesize sudden spike scenarios (1k tenants, 10 heavy) and measure tail for top 10 SLA tenants. track cost delta vs naive degrade.

maria: add a regression test: ensure gold p95 does not increase >10% in simulated spike while overall cost increase bounded (<25%). if fails, tune burst_multiplier.

kevin: rollout approach: 1) publish weight/epoch API + local token reservoir; 2) run offline sim; 3) small internal canary with non-pay customers; 4) 1-week progressive ramp and monitor runbook triggers.

lia: outstanding question: eviction ordering for requests sharing same slot cost (tie). simplest deterministic tie-breaker: compare (tenant_priority, oldest_request_ts, randomness_entropy). randomness_entropy should be tiny.

anne: security: logs must not include raw prompt text. store only root_trace_id and aggregated cost_estimate. make sure explain endpoint strips prompt fragments.

maria: action items: @sahil - implement hybrid slot+token prototype; @kevin - add cooldown + warmup hooks to runtime; @lia - update router perf contract doc; @anne - draft RFC with config schema + sim results. meet next Tue to review.

anne: thanks all. dropping RFC link when ready. :white_check_mark:
